- If sentiment is consistently negative (0.00) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- If sentiment spikes to 1.00 or 0.20 near end of history, model often overreacts with sharp upward forecasts; cap forecast at 10–15% below recent peak.
- After a sharp price drop (e.g., >5% in 3–5 days), model frequently undercorrects — add 1–3% upward bias to compensate for mean reversion.
- When history shows strong downward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive drops), model often fails to recognize continuation — apply downward bias of 3–7% for next 3–5 days.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, flag as “overshoot” — reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment is strongly bullish (1.00).
- If sentiment history shows no clear trend (mostly 0.00), model tends to drift toward historical mean — adjust forecast to align with 30-day rolling average of past 10–15 days.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows early sharp decline (first 5–7 days), model often misses it — reduce first 5 days’ forecast by 5–10% to avoid lagged reaction.
